newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hopes to visit Pakistan - Albright.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hopes to visit Pakistan - Albright.

text.p: President Bill Clinton hopes to visit Pakistan, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Thursday in a statement commemorating the 50th anniversary of Pakistan's independence from Britain.
Albright, due to visit Pakistan and India in November, said Clinton hoped to follow her visit with a trip of his own, but she did not give a timeframe for the presidential visit.

The White House on Monday said Clinton had been invited to India to celebrate its 50th anniversary of independence and wanted to go. In New Delhi, Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said Clinton had accepted his invitation to visit during year-long celebrations of the anniversary, which falls on Aug. 15.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry on Thursday repeated Clinton's desire to travel to South Asia, although he did not specifically mention Pakistan.

Albright quoted Clinton as saying in a message to the people of Pakistan that Washington valued the 50 years of friendship between the two nations, and that the United States "continued to view Pakistan as a key partner in advancing peace and prosperity in South Asia."

She said the United States and Pakistan enjoyed strong and growing economic ties, were cooperating on efforts to fight terrorism and drug trafficking, and she expected the relationship to continue improving over the next 50 years.

"I believe we can look forward with confidence to even closer cooperation in the half-century ahead -- beginning with my visit to Pakistan later this year, which the president hopes to follow with a visit of his own," she said in a statement on the day of celebrations to mark the 50 years that have passed since the Indian subcontinent was partitioned at the end of British rule in 1947.
"Those visits will both underline the strength of our relationship and serve to develop it further for a new century of prosperity and peace," Albright said.
Albright will be the first U.S. secretary of state to visit Pakistan and India since George Shultz in 1983.

Arms proliferation remains the key U.S. concern on the subcontinent and led to a diplomatic confrontation in 1996 when the United States and its allies defeated an attempt by India to block a global nuclear test ban treaty.

The Clinton administration is backing legislation in Congress that would restore some economic and military aid to Pakistan that has been blocked for years because of concerns over Islamabad's nuclear program.
